entities.summary:
Aeneas of Gaza was a Neo-Platonic philosopher and a convert to Christianity who flourished towards the end of the fifth century. He was born in Byzantine Palaestina, around 500 CE, and died in Gaza in 550 CE. Aeneas of Gaza was a key figure associated with the Rhetorical School of Gaza, which flourished in Byzantine Palaestina during the fifth and sixth centuries.

Aeneas of Gaza played a significant role in the spread of Christianity in the Eastern Roman Empire. He was one of the first Christian philosophers and wrote several treatises on Christian doctrine, including a commentary on the Gospel of John. His work was widely read and influential, particularly among the educated elite of the Eastern Roman Empire.

Aeneas of Gaza's legacy can be seen in the many Christian philosophers and theologians who followed in his footsteps. His ideas on the nature of God and the importance of reason in understanding religious doctrine continued to shape Christian thought for centuries to come.

Despite his significant contributions to Christian theology, Aeneas of Gaza remains a somewhat enigmatic figure. Little is known about his life, and much of his work has been lost to time. However, his impact on the development of Christian thought is undeniable.

The fact that Aeneas of Gaza was able to write so prolifically, despite the challenges of living under the Byzantine Empire, is a testament to the cultural and intellectual achievements of the Eastern Roman Empire during the 5th and 6th centuries.
